items.title: Scalars, tensor powers, the empty tensor, opposite algebras and finite sums
items.statement:
Fix the following conventions, used on this page and by the later Hopf and Hecke pages.

- $k$ is a field ([[def-field]]) and every vector space is a $k$-vector space ([[def-vector-space]]); $\otimes$ means $\otimes_k$.
- $V\otimes W$ is the tensor product of [[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]], with the $k$-vector-space structure of [[thm-commutative-ring-module-structure-on-a-tensor-product]] and unit and universal property as in [[thm-universal-property-of-module-tensor-products]]. Every element of $V\otimes W$ is a finite sum of elementary tensors $v\otimes w$.
- Tensor powers are left-associated: $V^{\otimes 0}:=k$, $V^{\otimes 1}:=V$ and $V^{\otimes n}:=(V^{\otimes(n-1)})\otimes V$ for $n\ge2$. The empty tensor $k$ is identified with the tensor unit through the isomorphisms of [[thm-unit-isomorphisms-for-module-tensor-products]].
- For an algebra $A$ over a commutative ring ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) the opposite algebra $A^{\mathrm{op}}$ has the same underlying set and structure map and product $a\cdot b:=ba$ ([[def-opposite-ring]]).
- Finite sums $\sum_{i\in I}x_i$ follow [[def-finite-sum-in-a-commutative-monoid]]; an empty sum is $0$.

Parentheses in iterated tensor products may be dropped only after [[lem-hh-tensor-coherence-on-elementary-tensors]] has been proved.
items.strategy: A conventions item: every displayed symbol names an already constructed published object, and the only substantive assertions are that $V\otimes W$ is a $k$-vector space and that elementary tensors span it, which are the cited published statements. The left-associated recursion is a definition by recursion on $n$, so no existence proof is owed; the well-definedness obligations that the conventions create for consumers (associativity and unit coherence of iterated tensor products) are discharged by [[lem-hh-tensor-coherence-on-elementary-tensors]], which is the recorded justifier of this definition.

references.title: Keith Conrad, Tensor products (University of Connecticut expository notes, 60 pp.)
references.locator: §§1–3, printed pp. 1–13: elementary tensors, general tensors as finite sums, and the universal property used to fix the conventions

items.title: Associator naturality, pentagon, unit triangle and symmetry hexagons on elementary tensors
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $L,M,N,X$ be $k$-vector spaces. Write $\alpha_{A,B,C}:(A\otimes B)\otimes C\to A\otimes(B\otimes C)$ for the associators of [[thm-symmetry-and-associativity-over-a-commutative-ring]], $\sigma_{A,B}$ for its symmetries, and $\lambda,\rho$ for the unit isomorphisms of [[thm-unit-isomorphisms-for-module-tensor-products]].

1. **Naturality.** $\alpha$ and $\sigma$ are natural in all variables: for linear maps the usual squares commute; the unit isomorphisms are natural as well.
2. **Pentagon.** $(\mathrm{id}_L\otimes\alpha_{M,N,X})\circ\alpha_{L,M\otimes N,X}\circ(\alpha_{L,M,N}\otimes\mathrm{id}_X)=\alpha_{L,M,N\otimes X}\circ\alpha_{L\otimes M,N,X}$ as maps $((L\otimes M)\otimes N)\otimes X\to L\otimes(M\otimes(N\otimes X))$.
3. **Unit triangle.** $(\mathrm{id}_M\otimes\lambda_N)\circ\alpha_{M,k,N}=\rho_M\otimes\mathrm{id}_N$ as maps $(M\otimes k)\otimes N\to M\otimes N$.
4. **First symmetry hexagon.** $\alpha_{L,N,M}\circ(\sigma_{N,L}\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)\circ\alpha^{-1}_{N,L,M}\circ\sigma_{L\otimes M,N}=(\mathrm{id}_L\otimes\sigma_{M,N})\circ\alpha_{L,M,N}$ as maps $((L\otimes M)\otimes N)\to L\otimes(N\otimes M)$.
5. **Second symmetry hexagon.** $\alpha^{-1}_{N,L,M}\circ\sigma_{L\otimes M,N}\circ\alpha^{-1}_{L,M,N}=(\sigma_{L,N}\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)\circ\alpha^{-1}_{L,N,M}\circ(\mathrm{id}_L\otimes\sigma_{M,N})$ as maps $L\otimes(M\otimes N)\to(N\otimes L)\otimes M$.

All five identities are equalities of $k$-linear maps between iterated tensor products.
items.strategy: Check every identity on elementary tensors and extend by linearity. For the pentagon both composites send an elementary tensor $((l\otimes m)\otimes n)\otimes x$ to $l\otimes(m\otimes(n\otimes x))$; the unit triangle sends $(m\otimes c)\otimes n$ to $m\otimes(cn)=cm\otimes n$ on both sides; the first hexagon sends $((l\otimes m)\otimes n)$ to $l\otimes(n\otimes m)$ along both routes, and the second sends $l\otimes(m\otimes n)$ to $(n\otimes l)\otimes m$ along both routes. Naturality squares are checked on elementary tensors, where functoriality of $\otimes$ ([[prop-functoriality-of-module-tensor-products]]) computes both composites. Both sides of each diagram are $k$-linear maps on a tensor power, and elementary tensors span it ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]), so agreement on elementary tensors proves each identity. No general monoidal coherence theorem is invoked.

items.title: Tensoring injections and the kernel of a tensor product of quotient maps over a field
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field, let $f:V\to V'$ be an injective linear map and let $W$ be a $k$-vector space. Then $f\otimes\mathrm{id}_W:V\otimes W\to V'\otimes W$ is injective. Moreover, if $U\subseteq V$ and $Z\subseteq W$ are subspaces and $p:V\to V/U$, $q:W\to W/Z$ are the quotient maps, then, viewing $U\otimes W$ and $V\otimes Z$ as subspaces of $V\otimes W$ through the injections of the first part and the inclusions $U\subseteq V$, $Z\subseteq W$,
$$\ker(p\otimes q)=U\otimes W+V\otimes Z .$$
items.strategy:
1.1 Injectivity: by [[cor-a-linear-subspace-has-a-complement]] write $V'=f(V)\oplus C$ and define the linear map $g:V'\to V$ by $g(f(v))=v$ and $g(C)=0$. Functoriality ([[prop-functoriality-of-module-tensor-products]]) gives $(g\otimes\mathrm{id}_W)\circ(f\otimes\mathrm{id}_W)=(g\circ f)\otimes\mathrm{id}_W=\mathrm{id}_{V\otimes W}$, so $f\otimes\mathrm{id}_W$ is injective.
2.1 Kernel: write $V=U\oplus V_1$ and $W=Z\oplus W_1$ as direct sums of linear subspaces. Then $V/U\cong V_1$ and $W/Z\cong W_1$ by [[thm-second-isomorphism-theorem-modules]] applied to the first inclusions.
3.1 Distributivity of $\otimes$ over direct sums ([[thm-tensor-products-commute-with-arbitrary-direct-sums]]) and the unit isomorphisms give $$V\otimes W\cong(U\otimes W)\oplus(V_1\otimes Z)\oplus(V_1\otimes W_1),$$ where the first summand groups $U\otimes W=U\otimes Z\oplus U\otimes W_1$ via the unit isomorphisms; under this identification $p\otimes q$ is zero on $U\otimes W$, zero on $V_1\otimes Z$ and the canonical isomorphism $V_1\otimes W_1\to(V/U)\otimes(W/Z)$ on the last summand.
4.1 Hence $\ker(p\otimes q)=U\otimes W\oplus V_1\otimes Z$ inside the decomposition. Since the image of $U\otimes Z\to V\otimes W$ lies in the image of $U\otimes W\to V\otimes W$ (both are induced by the inclusions $U\subseteq V$, $Z\subseteq W$), $U\otimes W+V\otimes Z=U\otimes W\oplus V_1\otimes Z$, which is the kernel.

items.title: Coefficient separation for an independent family of vectors, with explicit Choice assumptions
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $v_1,\dots,v_n\in V$ be linearly independent vectors in a $k$-vector space $V$ and let $w_1,\dots,w_n\in W$ satisfy $\sum_{i=1}^n v_i\otimes w_i=0$ in $V\otimes W$. Then $w_i=0$ for every $i$; equivalently, the linear map $W^n\to V\otimes W$, $(w_i)\mapsto\sum_iv_i\otimes w_i$, is injective.

If $V$ is finite-dimensional the same conclusion is proved without the Axiom of Choice.
items.strategy: Assume AC and set $V_0=\mathrm{span}(v_1,\dots,v_n)$. By [[lem-hh-tensor-injections-quotients-and-kernels-over-a-field]] the inclusion $V_0\hookrightarrow V$ tensored with $\mathrm{id}_W$ is injective, so $\sum_iv_i\otimes w_i=0$ already in $V_0\otimes W$. Extend the independent list $(v_i)$ to a basis of $V_0$ ([[thm-dimension-of-a-linear-subspace]], no choice needed in finite dimension) and let $\varphi_i:V_0\to k$ be the coordinate functionals with $\varphi_i(v_j)=\delta_{ij}$ ([[thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis]]). The maps $\varphi_i\otimes\mathrm{id}_W$ are well defined by [[prop-functoriality-of-module-tensor-products]], and applying them to the relation gives $0=(\varphi_i\otimes\mathrm{id}_W)(\sum_jv_j\otimes w_j)=\sum_j\delta_{ij}w_j=w_i$. When $V$ is finite-dimensional, extend the list directly to a basis of $V$ instead and repeat the contraction; no complement selection, and hence no AC, is used.

references.title: Keith Conrad, Tensor products (University of Connecticut expository notes, 60 pp.)
references.locator: Theorem 4.15, printed pp. 18–19: uniqueness of coefficients in a tensor product with a free factor

items.axiom_use: In infinite dimension AC enters only through the injection lemma [[lem-hh-tensor-injections-quotients-and-kernels-over-a-field]], applied to the inclusion of the span of the independent list; the finite-dimensional case uses only the choice-free basis extension and is choice-free.

items.title: Finite tensor duality and basis-independent coevaluation
items.statement:
Let $V,W$ be finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces.

1. The bilinear map $V^*\times W^*\to(V\otimes W)^*$, $(f,g)\mapsto[v\otimes w\mapsto f(v)g(w)]$, induces an isomorphism $V^*\otimes W^*\to(V\otimes W)^*$. For ordered bases $(v_1,\dots,v_m)$ of $V$, $(w_1,\dots,w_n)$ of $W$ with dual bases $(v_i^*)$, $(w_j^*)$, the image of $v_i^*\otimes w_j^*$ is the dual basis vector of $v_i\otimes w_j$ in the product basis of $V\otimes W$.
2. For every ordered basis $(v_1,\dots,v_n)$ of $V$ the element $\sum_{i=1}^nv_i^*\otimes v_i\in V^*\otimes V$ is independent of the basis and corresponds to $\mathrm{id}_V$ under the isomorphism $V^*\otimes V\to\operatorname{Hom}(V,V)$, $f\otimes v\mapsto[x\mapsto f(x)v]$ ([[thm-hom-from-a-finite-dimensional-space-as-a-tensor-product]]). Its image under $\sigma_{V^*,V}$ is the corresponding element $\sum_iv_i\otimes v_i^*$ of $V\otimes V^*$.
3. The evaluation $\mathrm{ev}:V^*\otimes V\to k$, $f\otimes v\mapsto f(v)$, and the coevaluation $\mathrm{coev}:k\to V\otimes V^*$, $1\mapsto\sum_iv_i\otimes v_i^*$, are independent of the basis and satisfy $(\mathrm{id}_V\otimes\mathrm{ev})\circ\alpha_{V,V^*,V}\circ(\mathrm{coev}\otimes\mathrm{id}_V)=\mathrm{id}_V$ and $(\mathrm{ev}\otimes\mathrm{id}_{V^*})\circ\alpha^{-1}_{V^*,V,V^*}\circ(\mathrm{id}_{V^*}\otimes\mathrm{coev})=\mathrm{id}_{V^*}$, the unit isomorphisms $k\otimes V\cong V$, $V\otimes k\cong V$ being understood.
items.strategy:
1.1 The product basis theorem ([[thm-tensor-product-basis-from-bases]]) makes $(v_i\otimes w_j)$ a basis of $V\otimes W$, so linear functionals on $V\otimes W$ are determined by their values on it. The element $v_i^*\otimes w_j^*$ maps to the functional with value $\delta_{(i,j),(k,l)}$ on $v_k\otimes w_l$, i.e. to the dual basis vector of the product basis; by [[thm-dual-family-is-a-basis-in-finite-dimension]] these dual vectors form a basis of $(V\otimes W)^*$, so the induced linear map is an isomorphism.
2.1 Let $T$ be the image of $\sum_iv_i^*\otimes v_i$; then $T(u)=\sum_iv_i^*(u)v_i=u$ for every $u$ ([[thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis]]), so $T=\mathrm{id}_V$; since the defining isomorphism is injective and $\mathrm{id}_V$ does not depend on the basis, neither does the element.
3.1 Evaluate the composites on a basis: $x\mapsto\sum_iv_i^*(x)v_i=x$ and $f\mapsto\sum_if(v_i)v_i^*=f$; each composite is linear, so evaluation on a basis proves the identity. The displayed associator and unit maps use the elementary-tensor formulas of [[thm-symmetry-and-associativity-over-a-commutative-ring]] and [[thm-unit-isomorphisms-for-module-tensor-products]]; no general coherence result is needed.

items.title: The free associative R-algebra on a set and descent of relations
items.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $S$ a set. There is a unital associative $R$-algebra $R\langle S\rangle$, the **free associative $R$-algebra on $S$**, whose underlying $R$-module is free on the set of finite words in $S$ (including the empty word), with product given on words by concatenation and extended $R$-bilinearly.

1. **Universal property.** For every $R$-algebra $A$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) and every map $S\to A$ there is a unique unital $R$-algebra homomorphism $R\langle S\rangle\to A$ extending it. When $R=k$ is a field and $S$ indexes a basis of a vector space $V$, $R\langle S\rangle$ reproduces the published tensor algebra $T(V)$ ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]).
2. **Two-sided ideal description.** For $E\subseteq R\langle S\rangle$ the two-sided ideal $(E)$ ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) is the set of finite sums $\sum_sa_se_sb_s$ with $a_s,b_s\in R\langle S\rangle$ and $e_s\in E$.
3. **Quotient universal property.** If $\varphi:R\langle S\rangle\to A$ is an $R$-algebra homomorphism killing $E$, then $\varphi$ factors uniquely through the quotient $R\langle S\rangle/(E)$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]); the quotient is the presented $R$-algebra with generators $S$ and relations $E$.
items.strategy:
1.1 Words: define a word in $S$ to be a function $n\to S$ for some natural number $n$ ([[def-the-set-of-functions-from-one-set-to-another]], [[def-natural-numbers]]); the empty word is the unique function $0\to S$. Concatenation is defined by the obvious case split on the two lengths and is associative with the empty word as neutral, because addition of natural numbers is associative with $0$ as neutral.
2.1 Let $F=R^{(\text{words})}$ be the free $R$-module on the word set ([[def-free-module-on-a-set-and-standard-basis]]). The rule $(\sum a_ww,\sum b_vv)\mapsto\sum a_wb_v\,wv$ on basis words is $R$-bilinear, so by [[thm-universal-property-of-module-tensor-products]] it descends to a linear map $F\otimes_RF\to F$; associativity and the unit are checked on basis words and extended by bilinearity, using [[lem-finite-sum-reindexing-and-fubini]] for the finite sums. This makes $R\langle S\rangle:=F$ a unital associative $R$-algebra with central structure map.
3.1 Universal property: given $\varphi_0:S\to A$, set $\widehat\varphi(s_1\cdots s_n)=\varphi_0(s_1)\cdots\varphi_0(s_n)$ and $\widehat\varphi(\text{empty})=1_A$, extended $R$-linearly through the free basis ([[thm-universal-property-of-free-modules]]). Multiplicativity is associativity in $A$, and the map is the unique extension on the spanning word basis.
4.1 The displayed set of finite sums is a two-sided ideal containing $E$ and lies in every two-sided ideal containing $E$ (both inclusions close under left and right multiplication); the quotient then inherits its structure map $R\to R\langle S\rangle/(E)$, and [[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]] gives the stated factorisation.

items.title: Presentation base change and transport of explicit bases to commutative specializations
items.statement:
Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $X$ be a set and let $R\langle X\rangle$ be the free $R$-algebra on $X$ ([[lem-hh-free-associative-ring-and-relations-descent]]).

1. There is a unique $S$-algebra isomorphism $S\otimes_RR\langle X\rangle\to S\langle X\rangle$ with $s\otimes x_{i_1}\cdots x_{i_n}\mapsto s\,x_{i_1}\cdots x_{i_n}$ on words; its inverse sends a word to $1\otimes$ that word.
2. If $I\subseteq R\langle X\rangle$ is a two-sided ideal, then there is a unique $S$-algebra isomorphism $S\otimes_R\bigl(R\langle X\rangle/I\bigr)\cong(S\otimes_RR\langle X\rangle)/\operatorname{im}(S\otimes_RI)$, sending $s\otimes(y+I)$ to $(s\otimes y)+\operatorname{im}(S\otimes_RI)$, the image ideal being generated by the images of the relations. No flatness or freeness of $S$ over $R$ is assumed.
3. If an $R$-algebra $A$ is free as an $R$-module with basis $(a_i)$, then $S\otimes_RA$ is a free $S$-module with basis $(1\otimes a_i)$. Consequently an explicitly constructed basis isomorphism of a presentation may be tensored with $S$ to give a basis in every commutative specialization.
items.strategy:
1.1 The assignment $s\otimes w\mapsto s\,w$ is well defined on the tensor product by [[thm-universal-property-of-module-tensor-products]] applied to the $R$-balanced map $(s,w)\mapsto sw$; it is an $S$-algebra homomorphism by [[thm-tensor-product-of-algebras-over-a-commutative-ring]] and multiplicativity of word concatenation. The word basis map $w\mapsto1\otimes w$ is an $S$-algebra homomorphism by the universal property of $S\langle X\rangle$; the two composites fix all words and hence are identities.
2.1 Tensoring the exact sequence $I\to R\langle X\rangle\to R\langle X\rangle/I\to0$ with $S$ over $R$ and applying [[thm-right-exactness-of-tensor-products]] identifies $S\otimes_R(R\langle X\rangle/I)$ with the quotient of $S\otimes_RR\langle X\rangle$ by the image of $S\otimes_RI$; combine with part 1.
3.1 Apply [[thm-tensor-product-basis-from-bases]] to the free $R$-modules $S$ (basis $(1_S)$) and $A$ (basis $(a_i)$).

items.title: Multivariate polynomial and Laurent rings over commutative rings, domains and fraction fields
items.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $n\ge0$.

1. **Multivariate polynomial ring.** The ring $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ of [[def-multivariate-polynomial-ring-by-iteration]] is a commutative $R$-algebra, free as an $R$-module on the monomials $x^\alpha=x_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots x_n^{\alpha_n}$ ($\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$), and for every commutative $R$-algebra $A$ and elements $a_1,\dots,a_n\in A$ there is a unique $R$-algebra homomorphism $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to A$ with $x_i\mapsto a_i$. If $R$ is an integral domain, so is $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$.
2. **Laurent polynomial ring.** The set $\Lambda_{R,n}$ of finitely supported functions $\mathbb Z^n\to R$ with coefficientwise addition and convolution $(ab)_\gamma=\sum_{\alpha+\beta=\gamma}a_\alpha b_\beta$ (summed only over the finite supports of $a$ and $b$) is a commutative $R$-algebra, free as an $R$-module on the monomials $x^\alpha$ ($\alpha\in\mathbb Z^n$); each $x_i$ is a unit. For every commutative $R$-algebra $A$ and units $u_1,\dots,u_n\in A$ there is a unique $R$-algebra homomorphism $\Lambda_{R,n}\to A$ with $x_i\mapsto u_i$. If $R$ is an integral domain, so is $\Lambda_{R,n}$; no domain assertion is made over a ring with zero divisors. Only finitely many variables are used; in applications to Coxeter systems with a finite generator set, $W$ may nevertheless be infinite.
3. **Fraction field.** If $R$ is an integral domain, then on pairs $(f,g)$ with $f,g\in\Lambda_{R,n}$ and $g\ne0$, the relation $(f,g)\sim(f',g')$ iff $fg'=f'g$ is an equivalence relation compatible with $(f,g)+(f',g'):=(fg'+f'g,gg')$ and $(f,g)(f',g'):=(ff',gg')$, and the quotient $K(\Lambda_{R,n})$ is a field containing $\Lambda_{R,n}$ through $f\mapsto[(f,1)]$. The same construction gives the fraction field of $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$.
items.strategy:
1.1 Induct on $n$ on the iterated construction ([[def-multivariate-polynomial-ring-by-iteration]]): the case $n=0$ is $R$, and the successor step adjoins one polynomial indeterminate using the coefficient-sequence representation of [[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]] and its universal property ([[thm-universal-property-of-a-polynomial-ring]]); the monomial basis and the universal property follow by induction, and domain inheritance is [[cor-multivariate-polynomial-ring-over-a-domain-is-a-domain]].
2.1 Well-definedness of convolution: finitely supported $a,b$ have bounded supports, so every coefficient of $ab$ is a finite sum ([[lem-finite-sum-reindexing-and-fubini]]); the ring axioms are verified coefficientwise exactly as for the univariate polynomial ring ([[thm-polynomial-ring-is-a-commutative-ring]]), now over the group $\mathbb Z^n$. The monomials are visibly an $R$-basis ([[def-free-module-on-a-set-and-standard-basis]]), and substitution of finite sums gives the universal property for units ([[thm-universal-property-of-a-polynomial-ring]] iterated).
2.2 Domain: order $\mathbb Z^n$ by a linear order compatible with addition and compare leading coefficients of nonzero $a,b$: the product has nonzero leading coefficient $\operatorname{lc}(a)\operatorname{lc}(b)$ because $R$ is a domain ([[def-zero-divisor-and-integral-domain]]).
3.1 The relation is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive (transitivity uses $gg'\ne0$ and cancellation in the domain); the class of $(f,1)$ is nonzero exactly when $f\ne0$, so $f\mapsto[(f,1)]$ is injective; addition and multiplication are well defined and satisfy the field axioms because the domain has no zero divisors ([[def-equivalence-relation]], [[def-zero-divisor-and-integral-domain]]).

items.title: Finite matrix and module preliminaries: right inverses, rank invariance, finite length and nilpotent trace
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field.

1. Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $M$ a free $R$-module of finite rank $n$ with basis $(e_0,\dots,e_{n-1})$, and let $v_0,\dots,v_{n-1}\in M$ span $M$. Then the coordinate matrix $A$ of $(v_0,\dots,v_{n-1})$ in the basis $(e_i)$ has a right inverse, $\det(A)$ is a unit of $R$, and $(v_0,\dots,v_{n-1})$ is a basis of $M$. The determinant is formed for $n\ge1$; for $n=0$ the module is the zero module and the empty family is its basis, with no determinant clause.
2. If $F\subseteq E$ is a field extension and $A\in M_{m\times n}(F)$, then the rank of $A$ over $F$ equals its rank over $E$.
3. Let $B$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-algebra and $N$ a finite-dimensional left $B$-module. A proper submodule has strictly smaller $k$-dimension, a maximal proper submodule of a nonzero finite-dimensional module exists by maximal dimension (no arbitrary Choice), and iterating produces a finite composition series of $N$ ([[def-composition-series-and-length-of-a-module]]); in particular $N$ has finite length.
4. If $S_1,\dots,S_m$ are simple $B$-modules and $N\subseteq S_1\oplus\cdots\oplus S_m$ is a submodule, then $N$ is isomorphic to a direct sum of a subfamily of the $S_i$, and $N$ has a complement in $S_1\oplus\cdots\oplus S_m$.
5. If $T:N\to N$ is $k$-linear with $T^r=0$ for some $r\ge1$, then $\operatorname{tr}(T)=0$ ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]).
items.strategy:
1.1 Write $v_j=\sum_ia_{ij}e_i$ and let $A=(a_{ij})$ be the coordinate matrix, so $A$ represents the linear map $R^n\to R^n$ whose image is $M$. Spanning gives, for each standard basis vector $e_i$, a preimage $b_i$ with $Ab_i=e_i$ (finitely many choices); $B=(b_1,\dots,b_n)$ satisfies $AB=I_n$. Hence $\det(A)\det(B)=1$ ([[thm-determinant-multiplicative]]), so $\det(A)$ is a unit and [[cor-square-matrix-invertible-iff-determinant-is-a-unit]] (via [[thm-adjugate-identity-over-a-commutative-ring]]) makes $A$ invertible; the columns of an invertible coordinate matrix are a basis.
2.1 An $F$-basis of the row space remains $E$-linearly independent in the $E$-row space (expand an $E$-dependence in an $F$-basis of the span of its coefficients) and remains $E$-spanning, since $E$-combinations of the rows are $E$-combinations of the $F$-basis; so the row ranks agree, and [[cor-matrix-rank-equals-the-rank-of-its-linear-map]] identifies them with the ranks.
3.1 A strict inclusion of submodules is a strict inclusion of subspaces, so it strictly decreases $\dim_k$; among the proper submodules of a nonzero finite-dimensional module, one of maximal $k$-dimension is maximal proper and is selected by a finite minimization over the natural numbers ([[thm-dimension-of-a-linear-subspace]]); repeating on the successive quotients terminates after $\dim_k$ steps and yields a composition series.
4.1 Induct on $m$. For $m\le1$ the claim is clear. Write $N\subseteq S\oplus M$ with $M=S_2\oplus\cdots\oplus S_m$. If $N\cap S\ne0$, then $N\cap S=S$, and every $n=s+u\in N$ has $u=n-s\in N\cap M$, so $N=S\oplus(N\cap M)$. If $N\cap S=0$, the projection $N\to M$ is injective and its image is a submodule of $M$, hence by induction isomorphic to a direct sum of a subfamily and complemented in $M$ by some $K$. The projection is then an isomorphism $N\to\pi(N)$ and $N$ is the graph of a linear map over $\pi(N)$, so $N\oplus(S\oplus K)=S\oplus M$. No Choice is used, since each step is a finite induction.
5.1 Take the filtration $0\subseteq\ker T\subseteq\ker T^2\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\ker T^r=N$ and extend bases of $\ker T^i$ successively to bases of $\ker T^{i+1}$ ([[thm-dimension-of-a-linear-subspace]] applies without Choice in finite dimension; [[thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis]]). In the resulting ordered basis, $T$ maps the $i$-th block into the span of the earlier blocks, so its matrix is strictly upper triangular; hence the sum of diagonal entries — the trace ([[def-trace-of-a-square-matrix]], [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]) — is $0$.

items.title: The left regular module and its tensor powers detect linear and tensor identities
items.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $A$ be a unital $R$-algebra ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]), with $A$ regarded as its left regular module.

1. For $a,b\in A$ one has $a=b$ if and only if $a\cdot1_A=b\cdot1_A$.
2. For $n\ge1$ the tensor power $A^{\otimes n}$ is a left $A$-module via $a\cdot(a_1\otimes\cdots\otimes a_n)=(aa_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes a_n$. If $a\cdot z=b\cdot z$ for all $z\in A^{\otimes n}$, then $a=b$; in particular the single element $1_A^{\otimes n}$ detects equality. The analogous statement holds for the right regular structure. The empty tensor power $A^{\otimes0}=R$ carries no canonical left $A$-module structure here, so no $n=0$ case is claimed.
3. For $n\ge1$, if $f,g:A^{\times n}\to M$ are $R$-multilinear and agree on every $n$-tuple, then the $R$-linear maps $A^{\otimes n}\to M$ they induce ([[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]) agree; conversely, agreement of the induced maps gives agreement on all pure tensors $a_1\otimes\cdots\otimes a_n$.
4. Descent warning: if $\pi:A\to A/I$ is a quotient of $R$-algebras ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]), the induced map $A^{\otimes n}\to(A/I)^{\otimes n}$ is surjective, but an identity between $R$-linear maps out of $(A/I)^{\otimes n}$ may be checked on images of pure tensors of $A$ only after those maps have been shown to be well defined on the quotient; surjectivity alone is not descent.
items.strategy:
1.1 Evaluate at $1_A$.
2.1 Evaluate at $1_A^{\otimes n}$, using $1_A\cdot1_A=1_A$; the right-handed statement is the mirror computation.
3.1 Both statements are the universal property of the tensor power ([[thm-universal-property-of-module-tensor-products]] iterated, [[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]): multilinear maps out of $A^{\times n}$ correspond to linear maps out of $A^{\otimes n}$, and pure tensors span $A^{\otimes n}$ ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]), so agreement of linear maps on pure tensors suffices.
4.1 The induced map is a composite of tensor products of the surjection $\pi$ and is surjective by [[thm-right-exactness-of-tensor-products]]. A map out of the quotient exists only through the quotient universal property, and its value on a class must be independent of the chosen representative; that is the descent obligation the warning records.

title: Tensor Coherence and Algebraic Descent — Examples

items.title: Many finite presentations of one tensor and the invariant contraction
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $\ne2$. Work in $V=W=k^2$ with $u=(1,0)$, $v=(0,1)$, $u'=(2,0)$ and $v'=(0,\tfrac12)$. Then $u\otimes v=u'\otimes v'$ in $k^2\otimes k^2$, although $(u,v)\ne(u',v')$. Consequently every $k$-bilinear form $B:k^2\times k^2\to k$ with $B(u,v)=1$ gives the value $1$ on **every** finite presentation of that tensor: if $\sum_lx_l\otimes y_l=u\otimes v$ then $\sum_lB(x_l,y_l)=1$. The contraction of a bilinear form against a tensor is therefore independent of the presentation.
items.strategy: $u'=2u$ and $v'=\tfrac12v$, so $u'\otimes v'=2u\otimes\tfrac12v=u\otimes v$ by bilinearity of the elementary tensor. The bilinear form descends to the unique linear functional $\overline B$ on $k^2\otimes k^2$ with $\overline B(x\otimes y)=B(x,y)$ ([[thm-universal-property-of-module-tensor-products]], [[prop-elementary-tensor-formulas-descend-exactly-when-balanced]]), and $\overline B(\sum_lx_l\otimes y_l)=\sum_lB(x_l,y_l)$ depends only on $\sum_lx_l\otimes y_l$, not on the presentation.

items.title: The pentagon on four named vectors in $k^2$
items.statement: Let $e_1,e_2$ be the standard basis of $k^2$ and put $l=e_1$, $m=e_1+e_2$, $n=2e_2$, $x=e_1-e_2$. Then in $k^2\otimes k^2\otimes k^2\otimes k^2$ the pentagon of [[lem-hh-tensor-coherence-on-elementary-tensors]] holds on $((l\otimes m)\otimes n)\otimes x$: the two composites $(\mathrm{id}\otimes\alpha)\circ\alpha\circ(\alpha\otimes\mathrm{id})$ and $\alpha\circ\alpha$ both send that element to $l\otimes(m\otimes(n\otimes x))$, i.e. to $e_1\otimes((e_1+e_2)\otimes(2e_2\otimes(e_1-e_2)))$.
items.strategy: Expand $l\otimes m=e_1\otimes e_1+e_1\otimes e_2$ and follow the two composites of the pentagon on the single elementary tensor $((l\otimes m)\otimes n)\otimes x$; the first associator moves the bracket right past $n$, the remaining moves place it past $x$, and both routes produce $l\otimes(m\otimes(n\otimes x))$. This is one explicit element of the general identity proved in [[lem-hh-tensor-coherence-on-elementary-tensors]].

items.title: The tensor quotient by a one-dimensional subspace and its kernel
items.statement: Let $V=k^2$ with standard basis $e_1,e_2$, let $U=ke_1\subseteq V$, let $W=k^2$ with standard basis $f_1,f_2$ and let $Z=kf_2\subseteq W$. Then $\ker(p\otimes q)=\operatorname{span}\{e_1\otimes f_1,\,e_1\otimes f_2,\,e_2\otimes f_2\}=U\otimes W+V\otimes Z$ inside $V\otimes W$, and $p\otimes q$ sends the basis tensor $e_2\otimes f_1$ to a basis element of $(V/U)\otimes(W/Z)\cong k\otimes k\cong k$; in particular $p\otimes q$ is surjective and $\dim\ker(p\otimes q)=\dim U\dim W+\dim V\dim Z-\dim U\dim Z=3$, as predicted by [[lem-hh-tensor-injections-quotients-and-kernels-over-a-field]].
items.strategy: $(e_i\otimes f_j)$ is the product basis of $V\otimes W$ ([[thm-tensor-product-basis-from-bases]]). The quotient map $p$ kills $e_1$ and fixes the class of $e_2$; $q$ kills $f_2$ and fixes the class of $f_1$; hence $p\otimes q$ kills exactly the three basis tensors $e_1\otimes f_1,e_1\otimes f_2,e_2\otimes f_2$ and is injective on the span of $e_2\otimes f_1$. The killed span is $U\otimes W+V\otimes Z$.

items.title: Finite coevaluation computed in two bases
items.statement: Let $V=k^2$ with standard basis $e_1,e_2$, and let $k$ have characteristic $\ne2$. For the second basis $b_1=e_1+e_2$, $b_2=e_1-e_2$ with dual basis $b_1^*=\tfrac12(e_1^*+e_2^*)$, $b_2^*=\tfrac12(e_1^*-e_2^*)$, the elements $\sum_ie_i\otimes e_i^*$ and $\sum_jb_j\otimes b_j^*$ of $V\otimes V^*$ are equal. Hence the coevaluation $\mathrm{coev}:k\to V\otimes V^*$ of [[lem-hh-finite-tensor-duality-and-canonical-coevaluation]] is computed by the same element in both bases, and the zigzag identities hold in both.
items.strategy: Expand $\sum_jb_j\otimes b_j^*=\tfrac12\bigl((e_1+e_2)\otimes(e_1^*+e_2^*)+(e_1-e_2)\otimes(e_1^*-e_2^*)\bigr)$ and cancel the cross terms, using characteristic $\ne2$: the result is $e_1\otimes e_1^*+e_2\otimes e_2^*$. This is the basis-independence asserted in [[lem-hh-finite-tensor-duality-and-canonical-coevaluation]], here checked on a second explicit basis.

items.title: An infinite-dimensional tensor-dual functional outside the image
items.statement: The finitely proved identification of [[lem-hh-finite-tensor-duality-and-canonical-coevaluation]], read without its finite-dimensional hypothesis, would say that the canonical map $V^*\otimes V^*\to(V\otimes V)^*$, $f\otimes g\mapsto[v\otimes w\mapsto f(v)g(w)]$, is surjective for every $k$-vector space $V$.
items.strategy: For any $V$, apply the tensor universal property twice to the bilinear rule $(f,g)\mapsto[v\otimes w\mapsto f(v)g(w)]$ to construct the canonical map, without a finite-dimensional assumption ([[def-hh-scalar-and-tensor-conventions]]). $(e_i\otimes e_j)$ is a basis of $V\otimes V$ ([[thm-tensor-product-basis-from-bases]]), so $L$ is well defined. Suppose $L=\sum_{s=1}^mf_s\otimes g_s$. For each $j$ the functional $v\mapsto L(v\otimes e_j)$ equals the coordinate functional $e_j^*$ (because $L(e_i\otimes e_j)=\delta_{ij}$), and it also equals $\sum_sg_s(e_j)f_s$. Thus the infinite independent family $(e_j^*)_{j\in I}$ ([[def-linear-independence]], [[def-linear-basis]]) lies in the finite-dimensional span of $f_1,\dots,f_m$, contradicting [[cor-independent-set-is-no-larger-than-a-finite-spanning-set]].
